question: How many cubic cm of water can a hemispherical container of radius 7 cm hold (rounded off to 2 decimal places) (use π = (22)/(7))?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of a hemisphere = (2/3) × π × r³

Substitute r = 7 cm: V = (2/3) × (22/7) × 7³

V = (2/3) × 22 × 49 = 2156 ÷ 3 = 718.666...

Rounding off to two decimal places, V ≈ 718.67 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 718.67 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the hemispherical container (r) = 7 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a hemisphere (V) = (2/3) × π × r³

 

 
 
 
• 
 r = 7 cm
 
• 
 7 cm
 Hemispherical Container

**Calculations:**

⇒ V = (2/3) × (22/7) × 7³

⇒ V = (2/3) × (22/7) × 343

⇒ V = (2/3) × 22 × 49

⇒ V = 2156 ÷ 3

⇒ V ≈ 718.666... cm³

⇒ V = 718.67 cm³ (rounded off to 2 decimal places)

**∴ The correct answer is 718.67 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The volume of a complete sphere is double the volume of a hemisphere and is calculated using V = (4/3) × π × r³.

Curved Surface Area of a Hemisphere

The outer curved surface area is half that of a sphere, given by the formula CSA = 2 × π × r².

Total Surface Area of a Hemisphere

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the flat circular base, resulting in the formula TSA = 3 × π × r².
